q: 1. In case of a direct vernier scale
options: smallest division is longer than smallest division of the main scale
graduations increase in the same direction
explain: In a direct vernier, the scale graduations increase in the same direction as the main scale, and $n$ vernier divisions equal $(n-1)$ main scale divisions.

q: 2. An 'are' is the unit of area of a square of side
explain: One 'are' is a metric unit of area equal to 100 square meters, which is the area of a square with 10-meter sides.

q: 3. If L is the measured length of a base line whose elevation is h above M.S.L. The necessary correction to reduce the base length to M.S.L. is
explain: The correction for elevation (to reduce to Mean Sea Level) is $C_h = Lh/R$, where R is the radius of the Earth.

q: 4. Chain survey method is most suitable
options: in fairly level and open area
for large scale plans required for industrial site
explain: Chain surveying is limited to small, open, and level areas where the area can be easily divided into a network of triangles.

q: 5. The principle of chain surveying is to divided the area into a number of
explain: Triangulation is the fundamental principle of chain surveying; a triangle is the only simple plane figure that can be plotted uniquely by measuring its sides only.

q: 6. For locating the locations of the individual points according to situation we resort to
explain: Offsets (both perpendicular and oblique) are used to locate the positions of objects relative to the main survey lines.

q: 7. The method of measuring distance by pacing is chiefly used in
explain: Pacing, being a rough and quick method of distance measurement, is chiefly used during preliminary reconnaissance surveys where high accuracy is not required.

q: 8. Cumulative error that occur in chaining are proportional to .............
explain: Cumulative errors (like incorrect tape length) increase directly with the length of the line (L), whereas compensating errors are proportional to √L.

q: 9. Direct ranging is possible only when the end stations are
options: located at highest points in the sea
explain: Direct ranging (fixing intermediate points on a line by eye alone) is possible only when the two end stations of the line are mutually intervisible.

q: 10. The error in measured length due to incorrect holding of chain is
explain: Incorrect holding of the chain (not exactly along the line) sometimes lengthens and sometimes shortens the measured length randomly, so it is classified as a compensating (accidental) error.

q: 11. If the chain line which runs along N-S direction is horizontal and the ground in E-W direction is sloping .............
options: it is possible to set offsets correctly on east side
it is possible to set offsets correctly on east side
it is not possible to set offsets correctly on west side
it is possible to set offsets correctly on both sides
explain: Slope in the transverse direction (perpendicular to the chain line) does not prevent the setting of offsets, though horizontal distances must be measured correctly.

q: 12. Perpendicularity of an offset may be judged by eye, if the length of the offset is .............
explain: Generally, for offsets shorter than 15m, the perpendicular can be estimated by eye without significant loss of accuracy for standard scales.

q: 13. The most accurate measurement of the length of a long survey lines is made by using?
explain: Electronic Distance Measuring (EDM) equipment provides the highest accuracy for measuring the length of long survey lines, superior to steel bands, invar tapes, or tacheometry.

q: 14. The error due to bad ranging is .............
explain: Bad ranging always makes the measured line longer than the true length, resulting in a cumulative positive error.

options: ties or check lines which are perpendicular to chain line
sets of minor instruments in chain surveying
chain lines which go out of alignment
explain: Offsets are lateral measurements taken from the main chain line to locate the positions of nearby features.

q: 16. The tension, at which the effects of pull and sag for a tape are neutralised, is known as .............
explain: Normal tension is the specific pull applied to a tape so that the increase in length due to pull equals the decrease in length due to sag.

q: 17. A line joining the apex of a triangle to some fixed point on the opposite side is called a .............
explain: A check line (or proof line) is used to verify the accuracy of the framework by measuring from a known vertex to a point on the opposite side.

q: 18. Distance between two neighboring brass rings is .............
explain: In a metric chain, brass rings are typically provided at every 1 meter interval for easy counting.

q: 19. When 1 cm on a map represents 10 m on the ground, the representative fraction of the scale is .............
explain: RF = Map Distance / Ground Distance = 1cm / 1000cm = 1/1000.

q: 20. The representative fraction 1/2500 means that the scale is .............
explain: 1/2500 means 1 cm on the map = 2500 cm on the ground. 2500 cm = 25 meters.

q: 21. The main object of running a tie line is .............
options: to check accuracy of the work
to take details of nearby objects
to take offsets for detailed surveying
explain: Tie lines are primarily used to pick up internal details of the area that are far from the main chain lines.

q: 22. The main difference between an optical square and prism square is .............
options: that optical square is more accurate than prism square
that no adjustment is required in a prism square since the angle between the reflecting surfaces cannot be changed
explain: While both use the principle of double reflection, the prism square is fixed and requires no adjustment compared to the mirrors in an optical square.

q: 23. The difference between the most probable value and its observed value is .............
explain: Residual error is the difference between the most probable value (MPV) and the actual measurement.

q: 24. Correction for Sag is always
explain: Since a sagging tape always measures a distance that is effectively longer than the true horizontal distance, the sag correction is always subtracted, i.e., it is always negative.

q: 25. One mile equals to
explain: Since a Gunter's chain is 66 feet long and one mile is 5280 feet, one mile equals 5280/66 = 80 Gunter's chains.

q: 26. The distances AC and BC are measured from two fixed points A and B whose distance AB is known. The point C is plotted by intersection. This method is generally adopted in .............
explain: Locating a point by measuring two linear distances from two known points is the fundamental principle of offset measurement in chain surveying.

q: 27. The systematic errors which persist and have regular effects in the performance of a survey operations, are due to .............
explain: Systematic errors (also called cumulative errors) follow a mathematical law and are often caused by faulty instrument adjustment (e.g., a tape that is too short).

q: 28. The method of reversal .............
options: is usually directed to examine whether a certain part is truly parallel or perpendicular to another
makes the erroneous relationship between parts evident
explain: Reversing the instrument (like face left/face right) doubles the instrumental error, making it clearly visible so it can be corrected or averaged out.

q: 29. The apparent error on reversal is .............
explain: When you reverse an instrument, the existing error is applied in the opposite direction, making the apparent gap between the two readings twice the actual error.

q: 30. During chaining along a straight line, the leader of the party has 4 arrows in his hand while the follower has 6. Distance of the follower from the starting point is .............
explain: The number of arrows held by the follower indicates the number of full chain lengths completed from the starting point.

q: 31. A metallic tape is made of .............
explain: Metallic tapes are made of waterproof linen reinforced with fine brass or copper wires to prevent stretching.

q: 32. A line joining some fixed points on the main survey lines, is called a .............
explain: A tie line joins fixed points on main lines to enable the location of interior details and to check the accuracy of the framework.

q: 33. A base line in a chain survey .............
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the survey or locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixes up the directions of all other lines
explain: The base line is the longest and most important line in a chain survey, providing the backbone for the entire framework and detail location.

q: 34. Chain surveying is most suitable when .............
options: area to be surveyed is small
ground is fairly level and open with simple details
plans are required on a large scale
explain: Chain surveying is limited by its simplicity; it is best for small, flat, uncomplicated areas where high-precision angular work isn't required.

q: 35. If L is the specified length of a tape, L1 its actual length and S the measured distance, then the true distance is given by the formula .............
explain: True Distance = (Actual Length / Nominal Length) x Measured Distance. If the tape is longer than specified, the recorded distance is too short, and vice versa.

q: 36. Metric chains are generally available in .............
explain: Standard IS metric chains are manufactured in lengths of 5, 10, 20, and 30 meters. 20m and 30m are the most common in field work.

q: 37. While measuring with a metallic tape of 30 m length pull should be applied .............
explain: A standard pull of about 3 kg (or 30 Newtons) is usually recommended for metallic tapes to counteract sag and ensure accuracy.

q: 38. A check line in a chain surveying .............
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the surveyor to locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixed up the directions of all other lines
explain: The sole purpose of a check line (proof line) is to verify the accuracy of the framework measurements during plotting.

q: 39. A tie line in a chain surveying .............
options: checks the accuracy of the framework
enables the surveyor to locate the interior details which are far away from the main chain lines
fixed up the directions of all other lines
explain: Tie lines are secondary lines used to pick up interior details that are too far from the main survey lines to be accurately measured by offsets.

q: 40. Then the position of a point is to be located accurately by a perpendicular offset, the direction of perpendicular is set out by means of .............
explain: An optical square is a small, portable instrument used for setting out right angles to a line with higher precision than a cross-staff.

q: 41. The accuracy in laying down the perpendicular offsets and in measuring them depends upon .............
explain: Accuracy requirements vary based on how small the scale of the map is, how far the point is from the chain line, and how critical the object is to the survey.

q: 42. The limiting length of the offset is ............. when its perpendicular direction is set out by an eye.
explain: When setting offsets by eye (without an instrument), the maximum length is generally restricted to 15m to keep the error within permissible limits.

q: 43. The instrument used for setting out an offset at a right angle, is called .............
explain: While cross-staffs can do this, the optical square is the specific high-accuracy choice among these options for 90-degree offsets.

q: 44. The adjustable cross-staff is used for setting out an offset .............
explain: An adjustable cross-staff consists of two cylinders that can be rotated relative to each other, allowing any angle to be set and observed.

q: 45. For setting out an offset at an angle 45°, ............. cross-staff is used.
explain: The French cross-staff is octagonal and has sights that allow angles of 45° and 90° to be set out.

q: 46. For the Abney clinometer the semi-circular arc is graduated as
explain: The Abney clinometer's arc is graduated from 0° at the center to 90° on either side to measure both angles of elevation and depression.

q: 47. To use the Abney clinometer as Abney level the vernier should read
options: it is not possible to use clinometer as hand level
explain: When the vernier is set to 0°, the line of sight becomes horizontal, allowing the clinometer to function as a basic hand level.

q: 48. A scale which has a common representative fraction, but read in different measures, is called a
explain: Comparative scales (or corresponding scales) have the same R.F. but graduate in different units, like miles and kilometers.

q: 49. In a direct vernier, the smallest division of a vernier is ............ the smallest division of its primary scale.
explain: In a direct vernier, $(n-1)$ divisions of the main scale are divided into $n$ divisions on the vernier, making each vernier division slightly shorter than a main scale division.

q: 50. Measurements taken with a wrong scale can be corrected by using the relation
options: true length = (correct scale / wrong scale) × measured length
true length = (correct scale / wrong scale)² × measured length
true length = (correct scale / wrong scale)³ × measured length
explain: Linear correction is proportional to the ratio of the scales. For area, the ratio would be squared; for volume, cubed.
